edges.notes: Image manifests and blobs are transported via registry HTTP APIs defined by the distribution spec.
Unpacked images yield a runtime bundle (rootfs + config.json) governed by the OCI Runtime Spec.
Docker Engine builds and runs OCI-compatible images; format standardized separately from Moby/dockerd.
containerd pulls, stores, and unpacks OCI images toward runtime bundles in typical CRI stacks.
OCI images are unpacked into OCI runtime bundles consumed by runc-class runtimes.
OCI images unpack into bundles executed by crun when configured as the low-level OCI runtime.
Workloads are commonly specified as container images pulled as OCI artifacts into node runtimes.
Overlapping 'ship runnable service tree' goal: OCI layers vs systemd portable OS-tree bundles; different tooling and hosts.
OCI layers target container roots; sysext merges extensions into host hierarchies under systemd — different format and activation path.
OCI config-in-image vs confext host /etc merge — different delivery and activation path.
Many published OCI images use Alpine-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use Debian-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use Ubuntu-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use Fedora-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use RHEL-derived or UBI rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use Rocky Linux-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use AlmaLinux-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many published OCI images use CentOS Stream-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
Many historical OCI images used CentOS Linux-derived rootfs layers; layout still conforms to OCI image spec.
OCI image layers define manifests and blobs; Linux hosts often unpack and mount with overlay, which is kernel behavior distinct from the image spec.
OCI image spec governs layer blobs and manifests; FUSE is a Linux filesystem bridge unrelated to image JSON law.
BuildKit builds and exports container images whose manifests and layers conform to OCI Image Spec layout.
Helm chart templates commonly reference workload container images that are pulled as OCI images.
Flux image automation reconciles workload image references as OCI images (tags/digests).
Argo CD Applications reference container images that are pulled as OCI images in typical deployments.
